subject: Finova - Performance SLOs & Multi-region routing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@finova.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Finova — Post-call recap: performance targets & next steps

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Key performance targets you shared:
- Latency (in-region): p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 150ms for single-request chat generation (streaming enabled)
- Cross-region (EU/US failover): p95 <= 200ms to EU from US users, p95 <= 250ms to APAC from US region (expected higher)
- Throughput: sustained 600 qps across peak hour (user-facing concurrent sessions ~1,200), burst to 1,500 qps for short windows
- Concurrency: typical per-instance concurrency target 40-80; client needs ~500 concurrent streaming sessions per region
- Streaming: token-level streaming is required for chat UX; must support partial tokens and early flushes

Data residency constraints:
- EU customer PII must remain in EU region; can we confirm Redwood Private or Dedicated options for EU-hosted traffic and storage?

Action items I propose:
1) Nikhil: confirm whether our p95 numbers hold with streaming enabled for the model variants we discussed and identify any recommended quantization profiles. Deliver: brief compatibility note + perf estimates by EOD Thu (8/12).
2) Sarah: share the attachment you mentioned (SLO spreadsheet + expected traffic split by region) - I attached our template (finova-slo-reqs.xlsx) for your convenience.
3) Schedule a technical working session with your platform team + Rishi (reliability) to validate routing/fallback policies and data residency constraints. 30-45m should suffice.

I pasted a short table of what we typically measure during an SLO qualification run:
- cold-start latency (p95)
- steady-state per-token latency (p50/p95)
- end-to-end user-observed TTFP (time-to-first-prompt) with streaming
- throughput until 95% CPU/GPU util
- KV cache hit rates for prefix-heavy workloads

Let me know times that work for the working session.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Patel <sarah.patel@finova.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Finova — Post-call recap: performance targets & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is great, and yes the recap matches our needs. A few clarifications and notes from our side:

- The p95 targets are end-to-end from our web gateway to the text generation endpoint (so include network and any proxy layers). We will aim to measure from the EU and APAC regions separately.
- Traffic split (approx): US 55%, EU 30%, APAC 15% during peak. We will likely need EU-resident processing for EU accounts holding EU PII - storage and inference must remain within the EU for those tenants.
- For streaming: we require sub-200ms time-to-first-byte for the majority (p50) and reasonable p95 across regions - we understand APAC will be higher but want to baseline.
- We use a model variant that is ~26B and expect average 150 tokens per request for chat sessions.

Attached: our filled SLO sheet and a quick network diagram (network-topology.png).

Next steps from Finova: can you confirm if Dedicated EU capacity with our VPC peering + KMS integration is required to meet residency? Also please confirm if Redwood's routing can pin customers to EU model endpoints but fail over to US for non-PII traffic.

I can do a working session Thursday 11:00-11:45 PT or Friday 08:00-08:45 PT.

Sarah Patel
Head of Platform
Finova Bank
sarah.patel@finova.com

Attachments: finova-slo-reqs-complete.xlsx (15KB), network-topology.png (48KB)

Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 07:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finova — Post-call recap: performance targets & next steps

Sarah - thanks for the additional details and the sheet. Looping in Nikhil and Rishi for technical confirmation. See inline responses and proposed timelines below.

Inline answers/high level:
- Dedicated EU capacity + VPC peering + KMS: yes, that is the recommended path to guarantee EU data residency for both storage and inference. We can provision a Dedicated pool in the EU region and set a routing policy to pin EU tenant traffic to EU nodes.
- Failover behavior: routing policies can be configured to keep EU-PII flows in-region; for non-PII traffic we can set a fallback to US/Global pool with a configurable TTL for KV cache migration. We will document the exact failover flow in the runbook.
- Streaming and p95 with the 26B variant: Nikhil, can you confirm realistic p50/p95 numbers with streaming enabled (150 tokens avg) on our EU Dedicated config? We should include cold-start delta when containers scale up.

Nikhil: plan below - please confirm or adjust.
- Run a two-hour qualification run against a mirrored traffic profile: 55% US / 30% EU / 15% APAC, avg payload 150 tokens, mix of 60% streaming chat / 40% single-shot calls.
- Measure: p50/p95 end-to-end, TTFB for streaming, throughput until 90% GPU utilization, concurrency headroom.
- Deliverable: CSV of raw metrics + perf summary + suggested config (batching, quantization, concurrency limits) by EOD Thu (8/12).

Rishi: can you prepare the suggested routing policy (pin & fallback) and a draft runbook stub for data residency and audit logs?

Proposed working session: Thu 11:00 PT (30m) - invite sent. Will be a quick alignment + confirm test windows.

Thanks - I will also attach our perf-run template (see previous).
